title: onprem-encrypted-policy-mismatch-and-kube-proxy-interaction-journal-2027-03-15
content:
Summary:

Quick notes from initial sleuth session: an on-prem customer deployment reported periodic control-plane API timeouts and spikes in control-plane latency between 2027-03-15 02:10 UTC and 2027-03-15 09:40 UTC. Symptoms correlated with customer activating a new perimeter 'TLS inspection + NAT' policy on their edge firewall appliance. Attachments: packet captures, kube-proxy logs, conntrack export. This doc captures hypotheses, short-run mitigations, commands we ran, and an early draft runbook for future recurrence.

Impact observed:
- Kubernetes control-plane API (port 6443) observed 504s from kubelet healthchecks and flapping leader election attempts for several control-plane components.
- Some host-level agents reported TLS handshake failures (ALERT level) and retransmits.
- No lasting data loss; workloads continued once connection re-established but liveness probes caused pod churn on some nodes.

Initial hypothesis summary (ordered):
1) MTU/fragmentation introduced by TLS inspection + NAT device causing large TLS records to be fragmented and dropped — leads to retransmits and long RabbitMQ-style tails.
2) Stateful firewall doing symmetric NAT plus connection rewriting causing conntrack entries on nodes to diverge from control-plane source addressing (kube-proxy IPtables rules match failure).
3) Intermediate appliance doing TLS break/re-encrypt but mishandling TCP options (SACK/TS) causing packet reordering and retransmit storms.
4) Rare interaction: kube-proxy iptables connmark rewrite collides with firewall's SNAT pool leading to mismatched tuple and existing connections being refused.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2027-03-15 02:06: alerted: controlplane latency > 1s on 4 nodes (pager notification).
- 2027-03-15 02:10: customer reports change: deployed new edge policy "inspect-sni-nat-v2" via vendor UI at 02:05.
- 2027-03-15 02:14: captured first pcap fragment from node-node path (s3://redwood-pcaps/onprem-2027-03-15/controlplane-conn-trace.pcap).
- 2027-03-15 02:20: forced kube-proxy restart on node-3 to clear conntrack as mitigation test (reduced pod churn briefly).
- 2027-03-15 03:00: observed relapse with similar pattern; rollback of vendor policy temporarily restored stability.
- 2027-03-15 08:10: vendor released a firmware hotfix; customer applied at 08:00 — then observed sustained improvement by 08:40.

Key evidence snippets (extracted):
- tcpdump shows TLS record fragments with IP DF bit set and MTU path discovery failing (ICMP fragmentation-needed seen).
- conntrack export shows repeated CREATED/DESTROYed flows for same tuple with differing NAT translations on same node.
- kube-proxy logs: "Failed to sync endpoint X due to conntrack lookup failure: no matching entry" around spike windows.
- firewall logs (customer-provided): NAT pool rotation every 30s for high-port ephemeral mapping to maintain session affinity (aggressive).

Commands we executed (for reproducibility):
- sudo conntrack -L | grep 10.0.12.34 > /tmp/conntrack-before.txt
- sudo iptables-save > /tmp/iptables-before.txt
- tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/controlplane-frag.pcap 'tcp port 6443' & (captured async)
- sudo conntrack -D --orig-src 10.0.12.34 --orig-dst 10.0.0.5 --orig-port-src 56123 --orig-port-dst 6443  (manual cleanup on Node-3)
- curl -v --resolve api.internal:6443:10.0.0.5 https://api.internal:6443/healthz  (used to reproduce handshake failure)

Short-term mitigations applied and observations:
- Rolling restart of kube-proxy cleared stale conntrack on ~6 nodes; reduced immediate 504s but did not stop recurrence when policy re-applied.
- Instructed customer to temporarily disable SNAT rotation (vendor setting: ephemeral-pool-ttl=0). After disabling, observed immediate decrease in conntrack churn.
- Suggested to set MSS clamping on edge device to 1350 to avoid fragmentation; customer applied and fragmentation ICMPs dropped from capture.

Root cause (current working conclusion):
The customer edge appliance combination of TLS inspection + aggressive SNAT rotation exposed a latent sensitivity in our on-prem kube-proxy conntrack assumptions: rewritten source addresses combined with path MTU mismatches produced duplicate/misaligned conntrack tuples and fragmented TLS records. Kube-proxy's reliance on stable 5-tuple for NAT/matching led to repeated flow recreation and transient connection failures when NAT mapping changed mid-session.

Action items (near term):
- [SRE] Draft conservative runbook steps for similar incidents: ordered list included below. (owner: Maya)
- [Infra] Add conntrack metrics export to node-level dashboards (conntrack table size, create/destroy rates) (owner: Connor).
- [Solutions Eng] Coordinate with vendor to document recommended settings for inspect-sni-nat-v2 (Maya + Aisha) and push into customer onboarding docs.
- [Runtime] Investigate if kube-proxy can be hardened to tolerate NAT rotation by optionally matching on procfs socket hashes in addition to 5-tuple (owner: Diego; spike ticket GH-PR link above).
- [Security] Validate MSS clamping recommendation for all TLS-inspection flows doesn't violate corporate inspection policy.

Draft runbook (fast triage):
1) Pager fires for control-plane timeouts affecting on-prem cluster.
2) Triage: check node-level conntrack create/destroy spikes in the last 5m (node_exporter metrics: node_conntrack_creates_total, node_conntrack_destroys_total).
3) Ask customer: did you apply any edge/firewall/NAT/TLS inspection config in last 30 minutes? (Slack template below).
4) If yes, ask vendor to temporarily disable SNAT rotation and enable MSS clamp to 1350.
5) On cluster nodes: sudo conntrack -L | grep <control-plane-ip> to baseline. If churn > threshold (heuristic: 200 creates/s sustained), prepare to restart kube-proxy on affected nodes one at a time.
6) Coordinate with customer to roll back the last policy if mitigations don't hold.
7) Collect pcaps (tcpdump) before restarts and upload to s3 with timestamp.
8) After control plane stabilized, capture conntrack before/after and escalate to Runtime team with logs and pcap.

Investigation notes / unknowns for follow-up:
- Need to quantify what 'aggressive' SNAT rotation looks like (port churn rate) and build an alert rule when conntrack create/destroy rate is anomalous vs baseline.
- Evaluate whether newer kube-proxy or IPVS modes behave differently under NAT rotation. Quick test plan: spin up small lab cluster behind HA NAT with rotation and benchmark. (ticket: SRE-4525).
- Examine possibility of surfacing a per-tenant ingress hint in control-plane protocol (not likely short-term) so proxies can match on stable identifier rather than strict tuple.

Slack template for customer ask (copy-paste):
"Hi — we see elevated control-plane timeouts coinciding with the 'inspect-sni-nat-v2' policy push at ~{{time}}. Can you temporarily disable the SNAT rotation (ephemeral-pool-ttl) and enable MSS clamping to 1350? Also please share any vendor logs for NAT translation activity. If you prefer, we can schedule a short window to test toggles while we monitor. — Maya (SRE)"

Relevant artifacts and quick links:
- pcap archive: s3://redwood-pcaps/onprem-2027-03-15/controlplane-conn-trace.pcap
- kube-proxy logs (sample): /var/log/kube-proxy/kube-proxy.log.2027-03-15
- conntrack dump: /tmp/conntrack-before.txt and /tmp/conntrack-after.txt (attached to JIRA-SRE-4521)
- vendor firmware release notes: https://vendor.example.com/relnotes/inspect-sni-nat-v2-1.0.7
- GH spike: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane-proxy/pull/1234

Follow-ups to schedule (owners):
- Lab reproduction with NAT rotation + TLS inspection (Connor & Diego) - due 2027-03-28.
- Add conntrack create/destroy alert to centralized SRE alerts (Maya) - due 2027-03-22.
- Update customer onboarding docs with recommended edge settings and include MSS/clamp guidance (Aisha) - due 2027-04-05.

Notes to self (loose):
- This feels like a class of failures that will grow as customers adopt middlebox TLS inspection; consider a proactive audit of existing on-prem customers for SNAT behaviour.
- If we can detect inconsistent NAT translations (tuple changes mid-session) we could auto-trigger a more graceful kube-proxy reconcilation rather than letting liveness probes evict pods.

End of journal.
